sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Which markers and host or parasite factors are linked to severity consistently, once severity definitions are aligned and each cohort is counted once? Input: the SV-G2 extraction of published group results (740 rows, 49 articles, 42 independent units, 131 canonical markers).

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: Each row was called significantly higher (H), lower (L), not significant (N), unclear or descriptive, relative to the worse outcome. Rows were merged into one call per independent unit (cohort in /core/cohorts.json, else the article) for each cell of marker x outcome class x species group. A cell is consistent when at least 2 tested units agree in one significant direction, at least two thirds of tested units agree, and no unit points the other way. Multivariable rows are kept apart.
Pooling was allowed only for 3 or more units with one species, one outcome class and a usable summary (Hedges g, Fisher z or log odds ratio; random effects with REML and the Hartung-Knapp interval).
Deviation D1, added after the primary result: the same matrix with all outcome classes of a species merged, as an exploratory direction table only (not pooled).

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: Primary (negative): of 423 cells, 15 have 2 tested units and none has 3 (largest 2). Nothing could be pooled: 2 cells had 2 units with usable summaries and none had 3. 3 cells are consistent in 2 units: Band neutrophils higher (mortality, B. rossi); Cortisol higher (other, B. rossi); Thyroid hormones lower (other, B. rossi).

D1 (exploratory): with outcome classes merged, 22 cells have 3 or more tested units. Consistent and not circular in 3 or more units: Body temperature (lower in severe, B. rossi, 3 of 4 tested units), Band neutrophils (higher in severe, B. rossi, 3 of 3 tested units), Cortisol (higher in severe, B. rossi, 3 of 3 tested units), Thyroid hormones (lower in severe, B. rossi, 3 of 3 tested units). Counting the Onderstepoort B. rossi units once (S1), 0 of these keep 3 agreeing units. Consistent but circular (the marker is part of the definition in at least one unit): ALP (B. canis), ALT (B. canis), Creatinine (B. canis), Urea (B. canis), Bilirubin (B. canis), Haematocrit/PCV (B. canis), AST (B. canis), Urea (B. rossi).

Named conflicts: no conflict in the extracted evidence: IL-8, Fibrinogen, aPTT, MDA, SOD and catalase, Parasitaemia, Platelets against death, Lactate, MCP-1 (candidate, SV-04). No two independent units in the extraction report one of these markers in opposite significant directions; the conflicts in the syntheses rest on comparisons with healthy controls, on articles that were not extracted (CB037 for IL-8 is abstract only), or on a significant result in one unit against a non-significant one in another.

Opposite significant directions between units occur in 2 primary cells: GGT (severity_grade, B. canis: CB307:H;CH12:L); Haematocrit/PCV (mortality, B. rossi: CB040:H;CB052:D;CH03:L). Haematocrit against death in B. rossi is a definition effect: CB040's significant row is the small haemoconcentration category, CH03's is lower haematocrit in non-survivors.
Selective reporting check: 0.50 of tested rows are not significant (median by article 0.53); 6 of 36 articles report no non-significant row.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: Direction counts are not effect sizes, and an absent cell is not evidence of no effect: most markers were tested in one unit for one definition. Species is aliased with source, country, assay and definition; species groups are never compared. Death includes euthanasia for poor prognosis in 11 of 18 mortality definitions (6 do not say). The D1 table mixes definitions and is exploratory; it was added after the primary result was known. Categories and calls come from language-model extraction with a 16-article owner check, not a full human review.
